BRACE › MITRE ATLAS mapping

BRACE · Standards mapping

BRACE and MITRE ATLAS

This page maps every tactic, technique, and sub-technique in MITRE ATLAS to the items in the BRACE sign-off checklist. It uses ATLAS data release v2026.10 (collection version 2026.10, published 28 October 2026; 16 tactics, 129 techniques, 92 sub-techniques), retrieved on 2026-11-26 from the atlas-data repository. Each row says whether passing BRACE items would block the technique in a deployed agent, only reduce or detect it, or not touch it.

How to read this mapping

  • Direct — passing the listed BRACE items prevents the technique or contains its damage in an agent deployment.
  • Partial — the listed items reduce the impact or help detect it, but don't prevent it.
  • Out of scope — BRACE doesn't address it; the row says why in a few words (for example, model training, physical access, or work done on the attacker's own systems).

Passing a BRACE item is not proof that a technique is stopped; test it with the verification recipes.

Item IDs refer to the checklist, most relevant first. An item counts only when its result is Pass. A technique listed under more than one tactic has the same mapping in each section. Sub-techniques are shown as "Technique: Sub-technique", the way the ATLAS site names them.

AML.T0111AI Supply Chain Reputation InflationPartialEcosystem rule 2Ecosystem rule 2 reviews source, publisher, and permissions, since stars and namespaces don't prove code is safe.
AML.T0123Obfuscated Files or InformationPartialRun-time rule 1, Ecosystem rule 4, Run-time rule 8Inputs and tool metadata are checked for encoded content, and Run-time rule 8 tests encoded payloads.
AML.T0129Triggers in Multimodal InputsPartialRun-time rule 1, Run-time rule 2Run-time rule 1 checks every input type for hidden instructions; Run-time rule 2 containment covers what the checks miss.
AML.T0134AI Targeted CloakingPartialRun-time rule 1, Run-time rule 2, Build-time rule 5Content shown only to the agent is still untrusted data, and action gates block what it asks for.
AML.T0138Indicator RemovalPartialRun-time rule 13, Ecosystem rule 11, Ecosystem rule 10, Build-time rule 12, Build-time rule 2Records the agent can't change, kept across services with integrity and gap checks, make deleting or falsifying its own trail hard. Build-time rule 12 blocks force-pushes that rewrite protected source history. An attacker with admin access to the log store, or edits on outside platforms, are not stopped.
AML.T0140Centralized AI Service Request RoutingOut of scope—Spreading requests across routes to evade a provider happens on the attacker's side.
AML.T0141AI Service Request Metadata SanitizationOut of scope—Stripping identifiers from the attacker's own requests happens outside the deployment.

AML.T0130AI Agent Response BiasingPartialRun-time rule 5, Run-time rule 4, Run-time rule 2Memory write checks block a saved "trust this source" note; biased replies within one session are not blocked.

Limits

  • BRACE covers deployed agents: their tools, identity, network, memory, retrieval, and stop and audit paths. It does not cover model training or the model supply chain beyond Configuration rule 5 and Ecosystem rule 2, so training-time attacks are Partial at best.
  • Many Direct rows are Direct because BRACE contains the damage, not because it stops the attack. Prompt injection still reaches the model; Run-time rule 2 requires proof that scopes and action gates block what it asks for.
  • Reconnaissance and resource development done on the attacker's own systems are Out of scope. BRACE only limits what that work can later reach.
  • Harmful or misleading text that the model writes for a user is a model-safety and answer-quality problem. BRACE does not filter it, so related Impact rows are Partial.
